title: Priority queue + lease deconfliction for console metrics pipeline
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a priority-aware, lease-deconflicted streaming processor for console metrics ingest. The goal is to ensure P0/P1 customer events and operational signals are processed with strict latency bounds while preserving fairness across tenants during overload. This ticket contains the design, spike results, and integration plan for a two-lane ingest model with distributed lease management and graceful backpressure behavior.
design_decisions: Two logical lanes per topic: HOT (P0) and STANDARD (P1+). HOT lane prioritized for latency-sensitive events (alerts, SLO violations, admin actions).
Use existing Kafka cluster for persisted hot/standard lanes (separate topics). This keeps retention and replay semantics and avoids introducing a new system.

Worker lease coordination implemented via our existing etcd cluster using ephemeral leases and a lightweight lease manager library to avoid split-brain claims. Leases are time-limited (30s) with renewals every 10s.
Per-tenant leaky-bucket token bucket at ingress to enforce fairness and prevent a single tenant from filling the HOT lane. Tokens refilled with tenant-configurable rates stored in PostgreSQL.
Local worker buffering uses a bounded priority heap with adaptive admission that drops low-priority events under memory pressure, and exports drop metrics to the console.
Checkpoints persisted to RocksDB and periodic snapshots uploaded to S3 every 5 minutes for fast recovery; commit offsets to Kafka only after snapshot is persisted.
tradeoffs: Using separate Kafka topics simplifies isolation and retention tuning but increases the number of topics and operational cost.
Etcd leases provide simple strong coordination but add dependency on leader election latency; mitigated by short lease TTLs and fast renewal.

Persisting snapshots to S3 before committing offsets increases end-to-end latency for durability but reduces risk of duplicate processing during failover. We chose durability over lowest possible latency for HOT lane because data correctness for operational signals is higher priority.
updates: 2026-02-21: Spike completed comparing Redis Streams vs Kafka for hot lanes. Kafka chosen due to existing operational tooling and retention semantics. See spike notes in Confluence.
2026-02-28: Prototype of etcd lease manager implemented; basic claim/renew/relinquish flow working in local cluster. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/412

2026-03-05: Benchmarks on m5d.large show median HOT-lane P95 latency 18ms at 3k rps with token-bucket throttling enabled. Memory bounded buffering prevents OOM but drops ~0.4% of low-priority events at 5k rps. Logged to dashboard: grafana.redwood.internal/d/ingest/hot-lane-bench

2026-03-09: Design review with PM and SRE. Action items: add robust metrics for lease health, expose tenant throttling config in Console, and run a chaos experiment that restarts workers to validate snapshot recovery procedure.

2026-03-12: Implemented snapshot-to-S3 flow and added automated commit gating. Integration test added that simulates worker failure during commit window. Tests passing in CI. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/437
acceptance_criteria: HOT lane P95 latency under 50ms at target load (3k rps) for x-tenants staging cluster
Lease manager demonstrates no dual-claims in 1,000 fault-injection trials (chaos run), documented in runbook
Per-tenant token-bucket limits configurable from Console and enforced end-to-end
Snapshots persisted to S3 and offsets only committed after successful snapshot; recovery time from snapshot < 30s in staging
Operational dashboards for dropped events, lease renewal failures, and per-tenant throttle metrics are added to the Console
notes: SRE recommended a short TTL for leases to speed failover; we settled on 30s after trial runs with 10s heartbeats.
PM requested ability to temporarily increase HOT lane capacity per customer during incidents; added to scope as follow-up sub-issue.
Design feedback: consider a hybrid model where extremely high-volume tenants are routed to dedicated ingest shards. Raised as potential future work (ENG-XXXX).
Security: cross-tenant meter metrics exported must be sanitized; security review flagged telemetry fields with PII — masking required before dashboarding.
